claims.text: The initial almost-equiatomic FeCoNi alloy has an FCC structure.
The initial FeCoNi alloy has high saturation magnetization.
The initial FeCoNi alloy has low coercivity.
Controlled post-synthesis annealing will induce nanoscale chemical short-range order in equiatomic FeCoNi.
Controlled post-synthesis annealing will induce mild lattice distortions in equiatomic FeCoNi.
Suitable annealing conditions can induce short-range order without causing a full phase transformation or significant long-range ordering.
Chemical short-range order and lattice distortions will increase magnetocrystalline anisotropy.
The proposed local order and lattice distortions enhance spin-orbit-coupling effects.
The induced local order and lattice distortions will provide additional domain-wall pinning sites.
Increased anisotropy and domain-wall pinning will increase coercivity.
The annealed FeCoNi alloy will have statistically significantly greater coercivity than untreated equiatomic FCC FeCoNi.
The annealed FeCoNi alloy will have greater coercivity than previously studied FeCoNiPd and FeCoNiPt alloys.
The annealed alloy will retain high saturation magnetization.
The annealed alloy will retain configurational entropy of at least 1.0R.
The coercivity-enhancing effect applies only while the FCC structure is maintained and full long-range ordering is avoided.
Excessive thermal treatment that produces secondary phases or major ordering may negate the coercivity benefit or degrade magnetic properties.
